conventions.convention: Signature is (−,+,+,+); proper-time tangent U is future timelike with g(U,U)=−c². Along C² curves, C¹ tensor components are differentiated with connection terms on every index.
F-sharp is defined by g(F-sharp(v),w)=F(w,v). The right-handed spatial convention F_ij=epsilon_ijk B_k gives projected spin transport proportional to s×B.

Coefficient uniqueness holds only within the displayed two-term transport ansatz, with orthogonality preservation for all allowed data and pointwise rest-space matching; alpha=0 determines neither coefficient.

Body moments use SI units, componentwise integrals, and explicitly specified slices. Curved moments transport integrands along unique joining geodesics within a convex normal neighborhood; slice independence and evolution are not supplied.
MPD equations are adopted neutral test-body truncations. Higher moments require specified constitutive or transport laws; no uniform truncation error or global existence follows.
TD closure is local to invertible K with future timelike W=K-inverse p. The conserved momentum quantity mu has momentum units; rest mass is M=mu/c.
Positive-energy size estimates require integrable densities, e≥0, |j|≤e/c almost everywhere, bounded rest-frame support, and positive total energy.
For nonzero body spin, timelike-observer centroid shifts fill an open disk; its boundary radius is a supremum. Zero spin permits only zero shift.
BMT polarization s and angular-momentum moment s-star are independent quantities unless an additional identification is adopted.

The charge-size bound assumes an exact Coulomb exterior outside the positive material support radius and total energy equal to exterior energy plus a nonnegative remainder; spherical symmetry alone is insufficient.
The multipole remainder is componentwise in a fixed smooth trivialization; derivatives of the trivialization enter the Hessian bounds.
Countable Choice is inherited by the GR smooth-structure and connection interfaces; the BMT deductions expressly assume no full Axiom of Choice.

load_bearing.statement: Defines flat stress-energy moments and local curved moments using a specified hypersurface, inverse exponential position vector, and parallel transport to the representative event. These definitions assert neither slice independence nor MPD evolution.

Under its Countable Choice, Lorentzian, regularity and restricted transport hypotheses, d g(U,s)/dτ=alpha(1−a−b)kappa. When a+b=1, initial orthogonality and the constrained spin norm are preserved. For alpha≠0, universal orthogonality preservation and the stipulated pointwise rest-space matching give a=G and b=1−G; alpha=0 identifies neither coefficient.
Under the stated Lorentzian and regularity hypotheses, S^{ab}n_b=0 and DτS^{ab}=p^aU^b−p^bU^a+T^{ab} imply gamma>0 and c gamma p^a=(E_n/c)U^a+S^{ab}Dτn_b+T^{ab}n_b.

Under Countable Choice and the stated neutral pole-dipole equations, TD states with invertible K and future timelike W=K-inverse p satisfy KU=mc²p and U=cW/sqrt(−g(W,W)). The normalized formula defines a smooth local ODE on the specified open region, preserves an initially zero TD constraint, and preserves mu and S_ab S^{ab}/2 on that constraint. At S=0, p=(mu/c)U and both p and U are parallel.

Adopts Dτp^a=−R^a_bcd U^b S^{cd}/2 and DτS^{ab}=p^aU^b−p^bU^a for the neutral test-body pole-dipole model, with an additional specified observer SSC. Optional multipole models require explicit force, torque and retained-moment constitutive data.

For the stated integrable rest densities supported almost everywhere in the closed ball of radius ell>0, with e≥0, |j|≤e/c and E_0=∫e>0, M=E_0/c² and s-star=∫x×j satisfy |s-star|≤ell Mc, equivalently ell≥|s-star|/(Mc).

For the stated flat momentum-rest TD data, delta^a=S^{ab}n_b/(p·n) and S-prime=S−delta∧p preserve total angular momentum and give the observer SSC. The spatial shift is s-star×v/(Mc²); nonzero spin gives exactly the open perpendicular disk of radius |s-star|/(Mc), and zero spin gives only zero shift.
Under the specified static body, exact Coulomb exterior, positive support radius ell, M>0, and energy accounting Mc²=E_ext+E_rem with E_rem≥0, Mc²≥q²/(8π epsilon_0 ell) and ell≥q²/(8π epsilon_0 Mc²).

Under the adopted BMT and local-action hypotheses, derives Lorentz covariance, free and G=0 transport branches, and the displayed uniform-rest-magnetic-field solution. Independently, under the stipulated flat-body density and spin-moment hypotheses, derives the spin-size bound and open centroid disk without identifying polarization with body spin.

concerns.concern: The Statement defines b only on U containing the support ball but writes B=∫rho(y)b(y)d³y over all space. Outside U, b(y) is undefined even though rho vanishes almost everywhere there. Specify integration over the ball/U or zero extension of the product; the estimate is unaffected.

Clause (b) asserts that 'the coordinate-change rule makes the resulting measure independent of the parametrization' without identifying a change-of-variables supplier or showing the density transformation. The missing justification is the Gram-matrix identity G-prime=J-transpose G J, hence sqrt(det G-prime)=|det J|sqrt(det G), combined with the C¹ substitution theorem.

The final Remark says the zero-spin conclusion is 'not an inference from a vanishing norm', whereas step 2.1 explicitly uses TD rest-space positivity and the conserved zero norm to prove S remains zero, before applying the zero-spin closure. Qualify the Remark as excluding an inference from an unrestricted indefinite tensor norm alone.
